newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: London insurance body says considering derivatives.
newsitem.headline: London insurance body says considering derivatives.

text.p: Proposals to create derivative-based products to tackle the capital and pricing volatility across the insurance sector are being considered by a London insurance market trade association, an official told Reuters.

"We have been looking at derivatives for the last two years, and we hope to unveil something before the end of 1997," Marie-Louise Rossi, chief executive of the London International Insurance and Reinsurance Association (LIRMA), said on the eve of the start of its annual conference in Dublin on Tuesday.
Rossi said announcements would not be made for another few months, but indicated that LIRMA or a contracted third party might set up products for use by the London insurance market.
"John Stoker, a financial services consultant, has been looking at this for us. We are in the fourth stage of examining feasibility, but it is too early to make decisions," she said.

Early indications are that that the products would seek to mitigate the "insurance cycle", where the amount of insurance capital available varies from year to year. This fluctuation results from the loss experience of insurance companies 12 to 24 months earlier, which has a knock-on effect on the price of insurance.

Until now derivatives and other financial instruments have been looked at as a way of tapping traditional capital markets to bolster the ability of insurers to cope with a deluge of claims from a catastrophe.
One example was the launch in the U.S. last year of the Catastrophe Exchange (CATEX), encouraged by reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter, to allow insurers to exchange blocks of risk exposure.

Other initiatives have aimed at avoiding the tie-up of capital in reserves, such as the move by Swiss insurer Winterthur to issue bonds against exceptional claims levels in part of its European insurance portfolio.
"This initiative shows that LIRMA is in the forefront of development in the industry," Rossi said.
